title: The Hard Cover
premise: Elodie Montrose, a ghost negotiator who handles the cases governments deny, receives a call on an unregistered burner from a voice she buried years ago: her former partner, Daniel Voss, officially dead since the botched negotiation that haunts her career. Voss claims he faked his death to infiltrate a private security syndicate planning to stage a catastrophic 'accident' during an upcoming diplomatic summit, and he needs Elodie—untraceable, deniable—to help him stop it. As they work together, old love resurfaces against her duty to the agency that erased them both, and Elodie discovers the syndicate's inside man is her own handler, who has been feeding her failures to keep her broken and obedient. In the end, Elodie exposes the plot mid-summit by turning the syndicate's own negotiation tactics against them, sacrifices her invisibility forever by testifying publicly, and chooses Voss—not because duty releases her, but because she finally redefines what duty means.
about_author: M. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to strangers talk each other back from the edge. They write thrillers about people whose jobs require them to stay calm while everything burns.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Between deniable cases in a rain-soaked safehouse city, Elodie answers a burner phone that has no listed origin—and hears the voice of Daniel Voss, dead for three years. The beat is vertigo: grief interrupted mid-sentence.

chapters.title: One Failure Still on the Board
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present-day debrief with handler Marcus Hale. We learn of the Aldergate negotiation that killed hostages and Voss's reputation alike, and how Hale uses it as leverage. The beat is shame weaponized.

chapters.title: Proof of Life
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Hiding in plain sight inside the Halcyon Group, Voss explains via coded dead-drops why he vanished: he found plans for a summit 'accident' too clean to be accidental. The beat is paranoid resolve.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She agrees to meet Voss in a train station crowd, testing him with questions only the real Daniel could answer. He passes—but so does someone watching them. The beat is cautious rekindling shadowed by surveillance.

chapters.title: The Accident Calendar
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Voss shares stolen schematics: a gas main beneath the summit venue, permits signed by a shell company. Elodie maps the attack timeline against the official schedule. The beat is cold clarity—the countdown begins.

chapters.title: Handler's Hands
chapters.summary: Hale's POV, first time. He reports Elodie's burner activity to an unknown superior, revealing he has been curating her guilt for years. The beat is quiet corruption; the reader now knows what Elodie doesn't.

chapters.title: Old Language
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A night in a safehouse relearning each other's rhythms; love resurfaces but both flinch from it, bound by rules neither fully believes anymore. The beat is tenderness at war with self-protection.

chapters.title: The Deniable Asset
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He walks readers through Halcyon's machinery—contractors, laundered money, a boardroom that treats catastrophe as logistics. The beat is dread dressed as corporate normalcy.

chapters.title: Interference Pattern
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Her agency suddenly pulls her onto an unrelated case—a distraction timed too perfectly. She realizes someone inside is steering her. The beat is the first crack in trust.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A courier exchange goes wrong; a Halcyon cleaner tails Voss home. Elodie improvises a phone negotiation to talk the cleaner down—her first on-page display of genius under pressure. The beat is adrenaline sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Board Knows
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He risks everything to photograph the syndicate's decision log and learns the attack has a second layer: a scapegoat already chosen. The name is Elodie Montrose. The beat is betrayal foreshadowed.

chapters.title: The Scapegoat File
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She finds her own fabricated trail—payments, forged comms—already seeded in agency archives. Someone built her ruin in advance. The beat is icy horror: she was always meant to take the fall.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Glass House
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She confronts Hale with partial evidence; he deflects with paternal warmth and a veiled threat about Aldergate. The beat is a duel fought entirely in subtext.

chapters.title: Countdown Protocol
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With 72 hours to the summit, Voss confirms the strike team's insertion route; Elodie drafts a negotiation strategy to flip the triggerman rather than fight him. The beat is grim teamwork, love expressed as competence.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Ordered to eliminate both loose ends, Hale struggles—he genuinely cared for Elodie once—then chooses the syndicate. The beat is the banality of selling out.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A rendezvous becomes a trap; Voss takes a bullet covering her escape. She negotiates their way out at gunpoint, voice steady while her hands shake. The beat is terror transmuted into control.

chapters.title: The Triggerman
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, extended single scene. In a locked maintenance tunnel beneath the venue, Elodie talks to Renn, the man holding the detonator—grief, debt, and doubt peeled open one layer at a time. The beat is her masterpiece: empathy as a weapon.

chapters.title: Accident Averted, War Declared
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Renn stands down; the 'accident' fails silently, unnoticed by the world. But Hale triggers the scapegoat file, and Elodie's arrest warrant lands within the hour. The beat is victory curdling instantly.

chapters.title: Turn the Board
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Instead of running, she walks into the summit's security cordon and negotiates with the one person above Hale—an oversight commissioner—using Voss's evidence and her own surrender as collateral. The beat is audacity: making herself undeniable.

chapters.title: Hale's Last Negotiation
chapters.summary: Climax, Elodie's POV. Cornered, Hale takes hostages in the commission chamber—the negotiator's nightmare made literal. Elodie talks him down not with threats but with the truth of what he threw away, then watches him choose surrender over the gun. The beat is devastating catharsis.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Public hearings dismantle Halcyon; Elodie testifies under her real name, ending her invisibility by choice. Voss, legally resurrected, stands beside her. The beat is grief finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Off the Board
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. Months later, two people run a small private mediation practice—no agencies, no ghosts, no burners. When an unlisted number calls, they let it ring. The beat is peace earned, guarded, and chosen.
